strengths.item: The paper is well organized, with a clear progression from motivation and preliminaries to examples, method, experiments, and appendices.
The main text is visually easy to inspect in standard ICLR format, with consistent margins, readable body text, clear section hierarchy, and clean equations.
Algorithms 1 and 2 are visually prominent and generally legible, helping clarify the proposed value instantiation and aggregation procedures.
Figure captions are informative and connected to the surrounding narrative, especially for Figures 1 and 2.

weaknesses.item: Figures 1 and 2 compress substantial information into limited space; small annotations, legends, tick labels, and color bars make them harder to inspect at normal zoom.
Figure 1 relies partly on color-coded box encodings, which are useful but somewhat color-dependent.
Several pages contain dense small-type footnotes, which add visual heaviness and may slow reading.
Some algorithm input/output descriptions and equations are dense, though still readable.

dimension_review.evidence_summary: The PDF inspection found that pages 1–8 are generally readable and consistently formatted in ICLR style. Figure 1 on page 4 is conceptually clear and has an informative caption, but its matrix entries, annotations, and color bars are small and dense. Figure 2 on page 8 is informative but crowded, especially panel (c), with small axis labels, legends, tick labels, and bars. Algorithms 1 and 2 on pages 6–7 are legible and well separated from the text. Equations are mostly clean, though Equations 1 and 4 are somewhat dense. Footnotes on several pages are readable but visually heavy.
dimension_review.rationale: The presentation is good overall: the paper is understandable, well structured, and mostly easy for reviewers to follow and verify. The writing and layout appear polished, and the captions and algorithms support comprehension. However, the paper falls short of excellent presentation because key figures are crowded and require zooming, and some dense footnotes, notation, and algorithm descriptions reduce ease of inspection. These are minor-to-moderate presentation issues rather than major barriers, supporting a score of 3.
